title: An isomorphism of right adjoints determines a unique isomorphism of left adjoints compatible with the units
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$ two adjunctions with $L_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R_i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and units $\eta_1:\mathrm{id}\to R_1L_1$, $\eta_2:\mathrm{id}\to R_2L_2$, and let $\delta:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$ be a natural isomorphism. Then there is a unique natural transformation $c:L_1\to L_2$ such that $R_1(c_X)\circ\eta_{1,X}=\delta_{L_2X}\circ\eta_{2,X}:X\to R_1L_2X$ for every object $X$ of $\mathcal C$, and $c$ is a natural isomorphism. (In particular, for $R_1=R_2$ and $\delta=\mathrm{id}$: two left adjoints of one functor are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism carrying the one unit to the other.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints) and the Yoneda argument of its proof: a transformation between left adjoints corresponds bijectively to the transformation between right adjoints inducing the same maps on Hom sets

mathlib_match.how: a few Mathlib lemmas, one per clause: with Mathlib's adj₁ := (L₂ ⊣ R₂), adj₂ := (L₁ ⊣ R₁) and α := δ : R₂ ⟶ R₁, put c := (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm δ : L₁ ⟶ L₂ (conjugateEquiv, Mates.lean:275); unit_conjugateEquiv_symm (Mates.lean:311) reads η₂ ≫ δ_{L₂X} = η₁ ≫ R₁(c_X), the unit equation (existence); c is an isomorphism since δ is: c = ((conjugateIsoEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm (asIso δ)).hom (conjugateIsoEquiv, Mates.lean:425); uniqueness: R₁(c'_X) ∘ η₁_X = (L₁ ⊣ R₁).homEquiv _ _ c'_X (Adjunction.homEquiv_unit, Adjunction/Basic.lean:181) and homEquiv is a bijection, so c'_X = c_X for any c' satisfying the equation. The case R₁ = R₂, δ = id is Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq with unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (Adjunction/Unique.lean:36, :53).
